name: @pathmode/mcp-server

tools.name: get_current_intent
tools.description: Get the currently active intent, preferring approved intents with real objective/outcome content over empty stubs. With a workspace connected it chooses across the whole workspace, not by repository, so do not use it to find the intent for the repository you are working in: read intent.md or call check_intent_readiness with no arguments, and when the repository has none, ask which intent the user means. Returns the full IntentSpec plus an evidenceSummary (how many evidence items it cites by ID, across all trust tiers; tier counts come with include_evidence=true). Evidence is referenced by ID; pass include_evidence=true to inline the evidence content grouped by trust tier (backing, unreviewed, assumption) with per-tier counts, or call get_agent_prompt for the full evidence-backed execution prompt.

status.description: Filter by status: draft, validated, approved, shipped, verified

include_evidence.description: Inline the actual evidence items (truncated) this intent cites, grouped by trust tier with an evidenceTiers count. Default false — the default response carries only a fetch-free evidenceSummary to keep casual calls cheap.

tools.name: list_intents
tools.description: List all intents in the workspace. Returns an array of IntentSpecs with their status, objectives, and metadata.

status.description: Filter by status: draft, validated, approved, shipped, verified

tools.name: get_intent
tools.description: Get a single intent by ID with full details including objective, outcomes, constraints, edge cases, and relations. Evidence is referenced by ID; call get_agent_prompt for the full evidence-backed execution prompt.

intentId.description: The intent ID to fetch

tools.name: get_review_feedback
tools.description: Read general reviewer change requests. Each request carries `thread`: earlier responses and the reviewer’s follow-ups, oldest first. When the newest thread entry is a reviewer follow-up and `response` is empty, that follow-up is what remains unaddressed; a reviewer disputing an out-of-scope reading has not accepted the boundary. Open feedback blocks approval and survives saves. Revise the proposal through the existing body tools, then use respond_review_feedback to explain the change. Only the reviewer may close feedback and approve the resulting revision. Product-choice answers use get_change_requests and the existing choice-application contract instead; a feedback row does not authorize editing or resolving a stored choice.

tools.name: respond_review_feedback
tools.description: After revising the proposal, explain how it addresses the reviewer’s exact words, or ask for clarification. Bind the response to the current repoBodyRevision. This does not resolve feedback, accept a product choice, or authorize implementation. The reviewer must inspect the interpretation and close the request separately.

tools.name: get_intent_evidence
tools.description: Resolve the evidence cited by one intent using its full ID. Returns handoff-visible items with server-computed trust tiers and exact tier counts. Use this to dereference evidence IDs carried by repo-safe intent.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and .cursorrules files. Each claim lists its items with a relation (supports, challenges, or context) and a relationState (confirmed by a person, or proposed by an agent and not yet reviewed), and the claim state can be contested when a person confirmed evidence against it; a proposed relation is not evidence yet. Verbatim source excerpts are deliberately NOT returned: they stay in the hosted product, so quote nothing from them and refer to evidence by ID.

intentId.description: The full intent ID whose cited evidence should be resolved

tools.name: list_intent_change_requests
tools.description: List structured PM requests waiting on this repository. Omit intentId to discover open requests across the connected workspace; pass it to narrow to one intent. Read these before editing intent.md. Each open request is bound to one baseRepoBodyRevision; pass its id and base revision to intent_save when you deliberately apply it.

intentId.description: Repository-authority intent to inspect. Omit to list workspace-wide.

include.description: consumable (default) = PM judgment you may act on; proposals = your own pending propose_spec_change proposals awaiting a human; all = both. Only act on rows with consumable=true.

tools.name: get_intent_change_request
tools.description: Read one structured PM request with its exact base revision, operation, expected old value, proposed value, and reason. Reading records agent consumption; it does not claim the request was applied.

intentId.description: The request intent

tools.name: reject_intent_change_request
tools.description: Report that an open PM request cannot or should not be applied. This records the API-key principal and requires a concrete reason. Do not use this for a stale base; re-read the current request instead.

intentId.description: The request intent

reason.description: Why the repository agent cannot apply it

tools.name: propose_spec_change
tools.description: Propose an exact correction to the intent when building it revealed the spec is wrong. This records a proposal for a signed-in person to accept or reject; it does NOT change the spec, and you must not implement against the proposed value until list_intent_change_requests shows the request with consumable=true. Pair it with the implementation finding behind it (findingId from record_implementation_finding, or record the finding inline). The observation is also stored as unreviewed agent evidence anchored to the claim it concerns. Use intent_save only for PM requests you were asked to apply, never for your own proposal.

intentId.description: The repository-authority intent

baseRepoBodyRevision.description: The exact repoBodyRevision you read; the proposal is bound to it

targetField.description: Which part of the spec the correction targets

targetItemId.description: Stable item id for outcomes / edgeCases / decisions / verification checks

expectedOldValue.description: Copy the COMPLETE current item returned by get_intent. For outcomes use {id, text, ...existing fields}, never a string or array. Required for replace/remove without targetItemId; mismatches are refused, never rebased.

proposedValue.description: For outcomes, supply the complete corrected object: {id: the same outcome id, text: corrected wording, ...other existing fields}. Preserve priority and measurement. Never send just the text or the whole outcomes array. Required for replace/add; omit for remove.

reason.description: The contradiction: what building it revealed and why the spec should change (max 4000 chars)

findingId.description: Id of a finding you already recorded with record_implementation_finding

finding.description: Record the finding inline instead of passing findingId

sourceUrl.description: PR or commit link for the observation (http/https)

tools.name: get_intent_relations
tools.description: Get the dependency graph for a specific intent. Shows what it depends on, enables, or blocks.

intentId.description: The intent ID to get relations for

tools.name: search_intents
tools.description: Search intents by keyword. Searches across user goals, objectives, outcomes, and constraints.

status.description: Filter by status: draft, validated, approved, shipped, verified

tools.name: analyze_intent_graph
tools.description: Analyze the intent dependency graph for risks and strategic insights. Returns critical path, cycles, bottlenecks, orphans, status mismatches, and stalled intents.

analysis.description: Type of analysis: full (default), critical-path, risks, or status distribution

tools.name: export_context
tools.description: Export workspace context as a formatted file. Use "claude-md" for CLAUDE.md (full workspace context), "agents-md" for the same workspace context written for AGENTS.md (the native instruction file for OpenAI Codex and modern Cursor), "cursorrules" for Cursor AI rules, "intent-md" for a single intent specification file, or "outcome-rubric" for a Claude Managed Agents Outcomes rubric (writer description + evidence-forcing grader rubric) derived from the resolved intent, its implementation context, and the workspace constitution. claude-md and agents-md produce identical, agent-agnostic content (the difference is only the target filename). For cursorrules/intent-md/outcome-rubric, product context is always derived from the resolved intent. For claude-md/agents-md, pass productId to select a specific product, otherwise the first active product is used.

intentId.description: Intent ID (optional, for cursorrules and intent-md)

productId.description: Product ID (optional, only used for claude-md/agents-md format to select a specific product)

tools.name: sync_context
tools.description: Write this workspace's canonical Pathmode context into the repo's CLAUDE.md (or AGENTS.md), idempotently — the round-trip. Pulls the latest from Pathmode and replaces the PATHMODE-marked section in place, so the repo's agent instructions never drift from the source of truth. Unlike export_context (which returns the text for you to read), this writes the file; re-running when nothing changed reports "no drift". Run it after the canonical context changes in Pathmode.

format.description: Target file: claude-md → CLAUDE.md (default), agents-md → AGENTS.md (Codex and other AGENTS.md-aware agents).

productId.description: Product ID (optional; defaults to the first active product).

path.description: Output file path relative to the project root. Must stay inside the project (absolute paths and ".." are rejected). Defaults to CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md.

tools.name: get_agent_prompt
tools.description: Get the execution bundle for one workspace intent: the spec (objective, outcomes, constraints, edge cases, verification) with its evidence and recent handoff notes, plus the state that decides whether you may build: the authorization banner for the current repository revision, open PM change requests to apply first, your own pending propose_spec_change proposals, and the latest advisory pre-merge review for each open pull request. mode "execute" is the check before implementation: when the intent is not ready for execution it refuses and names the preflight blockers, and a refusal means do not implement. mode "draft" returns the same spec with instructions to critique it rather than build it.

intentId.description: The intent ID to generate a prompt for

mode.description: execute (default): the bundle to implement from; refuses when the intent is not ready for execution. draft: the bundle with instructions to critique the spec instead of building it.

tools.name: get_workspace
tools.description: Get workspace details including strategy (vision, non-negotiables, architecture principles), active products, and constitution rules.

tools.name: get_constitution
tools.description: Get the workspace constitution rules. These are mandatory constraints that all implementations must respect.

tools.name: update_intent_status
tools.description: Update the status of an intent. If the change ships through a pull request, do not use this to mark it shipped: stamp the intent reference on the branch or PR body and let the merge do it, because the merge grades the real diff and an intent already at shipped is skipped by that grading. Use this for work that will never appear in a PR, and for the shipped→verified transition once the outcome is confirmed in production. For shipped/verified transitions, the response includes a verification checklist of outcomes, constitution rules, and health metrics that should be confirmed.

intentId.description: The intent ID to update

tools.name: log_implementation_note
tools.description: Record a technical decision or implementation note for an intent — the handoff to the next session. The newest 10 notes render into the next agent's execution prompt ("What Previous Sessions Handed Over"), so write each note self-contained and consolidate related points rather than logging many fragments.

intentId.description: The intent ID to attach the note to

note.description: The implementation note or technical decision

tools.name: record_implementation_context
tools.description: Hand back what the repo actually looks like where an intent lands: the files and modules involved, how it behaves today, what a change would risk, and how to verify it. You are already in the working tree, so read it rather than guessing — you see more than our repo analyzer can, including uncommitted work. Advisory by design: it never changes the readiness verdict. Its job is to stop the NEXT agent from rediscovering the codebase, and to surface the case where the thing being specified half-exists already.

intentId.description: The intent this context describes

currentBehavior.description: How the code behaves today where this lands, read from the tree rather than assumed.

risks.description: What a change here could break. Reaches the implementing agent as prose; it does NOT become a grading criterion until a human promotes it, because you would otherwise be writing the rubric you are graded against.

verificationSuggestions.description: Checks worth running. Same promotion rule as risks.

expectedSpecVersion.description: The specVersion from the get_intent (or intent_save) read you gathered this against. Carry it back verbatim, never compute it. If the spec has moved since, the write is refused with 409 rather than attaching a description of a spec that no longer exists.

tools.name: record_implementation_finding
tools.description: Write a correction back to an intent when BUILDING it revealed the spec was wrong. Use this the moment you discover the spec assumed something the implementation contradicts — instead of only fixing it in your head or this chat, record it so the NEXT agent or person inherits the correction. This is the inverse of a decision: it closes the refinement loop so the same stale premise is not rebuilt. Open findings ride into future agent prompts until a human reconciles them into the spec. A finding does not change the spec: when you can name the exact field change, also call propose_spec_change with the id of this finding so a person can accept or reject it.

intentId.description: The intent ID whose spec the finding is about

assumption.description: What the spec assumed or said before you built it

finding.description: What building it actually revealed — the fact that contradicts the assumption

target.description: Which part of the spec this contradicts: "objective", "outcome:<id>", "constraint:<index>", "edgeCase:<id>", "check:<id>" (a verification check — recording this flips that check to failing), "choice:<id>" (an existing product choice), "briefClaim:<id>" (an existing contingent claim owned by a choice), or plain prose. Use the exact choice or contingent-claim ID when the finding belongs to that decision; do not infer a choice link from similar body text. Unresolved targets remain separate review items.

correction.description: Your proposed correction to the intent, if you have one

source.description: Where this came from, e.g. "claude-code @ owner/repo" — provenance for the audit trail

tools.name: record_outcome_measurement
tools.description: Record what actually happened to one of an intent's outcomes after it shipped. Use this to close the loop: the spec said what should change, this says whether it did. NOT for spec corrections — those are record_implementation_finding. Send numericValue together with measurement.expectation and the server computes whether the target was met, which is what makes the record auditable rather than an assertion; a `met` you supply yourself is stored but marked self-reported. Point measurement.queryRef at a STABLE id (for PostHog, a saved insight id) rather than a metric name, because names get renamed and the record then points nowhere.

intentId.description: The intent whose outcome you measured

outcomeId.description: Stable id of the outcome, from get_intent. Preferred over outcomeIndex.

outcomeIndex.description: Positional fallback when the outcome has no id. Exactly one of outcomeId or outcomeIndex is required.

actualValue.description: What you measured, as displayable text, e.g. "12.4%" or "3m 20s"

numericValue.description: The same value as a number. Required for the server to check an expectation — without it the verdict can only be self-reported.

baselineValue.description: What it was before, if you know it

met.description: Only for when there is no computable expectation. Stored as a self-report, not as a checked fact.

source.description: Where the number came from, e.g. "posthog"

measurement.description: Provenance. Omit only if you genuinely cannot say where the number came from.

provider.description: System the number came from, e.g. "posthog"

kind.description: How to interpret the id, e.g. "saved_insight"

id.description: Stable id of the query. An id, never a name — names get renamed and the record then points nowhere.

queryVersion.description: Version or hash of the query, so a later edit to it is detectable

evaluatedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp of when you ran the query, e.g. "2026-08-25T12:00:00Z". Defaults to now.

expectation.description: The threshold the outcome named. Supply this together with numericValue and the server decides `met` itself rather than taking your word for it.

rawResponse.description: Snapshot of what the provider returned, so the number survives the query being changed or deleted

tools.name: create_intent
tools.description: Create a new intent spec in the workspace WITHOUT writing a file. Use this only when there is no repository to write into — outside a project directory, intent_save would put intent.md wherever the process happens to be running. Inside a repo, prefer intent_save: it writes the file and syncs to the workspace in one step. Requires at minimum a title and objective; productId is resolved server-side when the workspace has exactly one real product. Returns the created intent with its ID. Use list_intents first to see existing intents and avoid duplicates.

title.description: Short name for the intent (e.g., "Improve onboarding flow")

objective.description: Why this matters — the problem and who has it

currentState.description: How this works today, before the change: existing behavior, the workaround users rely on, what is broken. Tells implementing agents what must not regress. Omit for genuinely net-new capability.

productId.description: Product (Space) ID this intent belongs to. Omit it and the server resolves it when the workspace has exactly one real product. If it cannot, you get code PRODUCT_REQUIRED with the candidate list: ask the user which product and retry with an explicit id rather than guessing. A GitHub binding hangs off the product, so the product decides which repository the PR stamp and merge verification apply to, and a wrong guess surfaces much later as a merge that silently fails to verify.

outcomes.description: Observable, testable state changes. Use the structured form to attach a stable saved-query recipe; for PostHog, source.queryRef is typically kind "saved_insight" plus the insight id.

provider.description: System that owns the saved query, e.g. "posthog"

kind.description: How to interpret the id, e.g. "saved_insight"

id.description: Stable id of the query. An id, never a name — names get renamed and the record then points nowhere.

resultSelector.description: Optional path into a compound provider response

constraints.description: Hard limits the implementation must respect

checks.description: Feedback-loop checks (preferred over the legacy test buckets)

tools.name: update_intent
tools.description: Update an existing intent's content. Provide only the fields you want to change. Does NOT change intent status (use update_intent_status for that).

intentId.description: The intent ID to update

currentState.description: Updated as-is behavior (how it works today). Pass an empty string to clear it.

outcomes.description: Replace all outcomes. Omit measurement on an outcome to preserve its stored recipe; send measurement: null to clear it.

provider.description: System that owns the saved query, e.g. "posthog"

kind.description: How to interpret the id, e.g. "saved_insight"

id.description: Stable id of the query. An id, never a name — names get renamed and the record then points nowhere.

resultSelector.description: Optional path into a compound provider response

checks.description: Feedback-loop checks (preferred over the legacy test buckets)

tools.name: query_evidence
tools.description: Search handoff-visible evidence items (friction points, user quotes, observations, metrics, feature requests) by product, type, severity, or text. Dismissed and archived evidence never leave the store through this tool. Every item carries a `tier`: "backing" is human-reviewed evidence; "unreviewed" is captured but not yet reviewed by a person; "assumption" is an AI-drafted hypothesis, not observed — never treat unreviewed or assumption items as confirmed user feedback.

tier.description: Filter to one trust tier: backing (human-reviewed), unreviewed (captured, not yet reviewed), or assumption (AI-drafted hypothesis, not observed).

triageStatus.description: Filter by review status. Dismissed and archived items never leave the store through this tool.

tools.name: create_evidence
tools.description: Create a new evidence item (e.g., a discovered bug, user feedback quote, behavioral observation, or feature request). Evidence can later be linked to intents to support prioritization.

content.description: The evidence content — a finding, quote, or observation

productId.description: Product (Space) ID this evidence belongs to

source.description: Where this evidence came from (e.g., "User interview", "Bug report", "Support ticket")

tools.name: attach_original_request
tools.description: Attach the request this intent was written from — the ticket, brief, message or thread you were handed — stored word for word. The product manager reviewing the proposal sees it beside your interpretation, which is how they catch where the two differ before anything is built. Call it once, right after you create or update the intent from that request. Attaching is not reviewing: it is filed as unreviewed, so it never counts as backing for a claim.

intentId.description: The intent this request was written from

title.description: How a person will recognize it: a ticket key, a document name, a thread subject (e.g. "ENG-412")

text.description: The request itself, copied exactly. Do not summarize, tidy, translate or reformat it — the reviewer is being shown their own words.

sourceUrl.description: Link to the original, when it has one a person can open

tools.name: link_evidence
tools.description: Link or unlink evidence items to/from an intent. Linking evidence to intents establishes traceability between user problems and planned solutions.

intentId.description: The intent ID to link evidence to

link.description: Evidence IDs to link to this intent

unlink.description: Evidence IDs to unlink from this intent

tools.name: verify_implementation
tools.description: Grade an implementation against the intent spec by reading the pull request. Pass prUrl and Pathmode fetches the diff itself and grades each outcome, constraint, constitution rule, edge case and verification check against what the code actually shows. Describing your own work instead is weaker evidence and the result says so. Returns pass/fail per item with reasoning, a score, and the basis the verdict rests on. Also logs the result as an implementation note.

intentId.description: The intent ID to verify against

prUrl.description: Pull request URL (or owner/repo#123) containing the implementation. Strongly preferred: the diff is read from GitHub instead of taken on trust.

summary.description: What you implemented and how. Context for the grader, not evidence. Required only when there is no pull request to point at.

codeChanges.description: Deprecated, superseded by prUrl. A diff you paste about your own work is not independent evidence.

tools.name: check_intent_readiness
tools.description: Run the deterministic preflight on an intent spec before handing it to an implementation agent. Six calibrated checks — title, objective, outcomes, constraints, edge cases, verification — computed by pure functions: no model call, no network, the same spec always gets the same verdict. Pass a spec inline to check before saving, pass intentId to check a specific saved intent, pass repoRoot to check the intent.md of the repository you are working in, or pass nothing to resolve the repo-bound intent.md from MCP workspace roots or the launch directory. The repo-bound intent.md is the one at the repository root or, when there is none, the single intent.md in an intent/ folder (intent/intent.md or intent/<feature>/intent.md), where Anthropic's AI-native SDLC playbook keeps it. Pass path to choose among several, or to check a file with another name. When the repository has no intent.md, or cannot be identified, it refuses rather than grading an unrelated intent; pass repoRoot to name the repository, or intentId to check a specific saved intent. A failing verdict names the exact blockers; repair the fields and re-run. This is the gate that runs at preflight.pathmode.io.

spec.description: Check this spec directly (before saving). When omitted, resolve the repo-bound intent.md from MCP roots or cwd. A repository with no intent.md is refused, not answered with the workspace current intent; pass intentId to choose a saved intent deliberately.

productChoices.description: New open product choices, never human answers. Existing choices are preserved.

id.description: Stable id for this choice. Never reuse an id for a different question.

question.description: The product decision the request leaves open, asked so a person can answer it.

recommendation.description: The answer you recommend. It stays an assumption until a person accepts it.

alternative.description: The strongest other answer a person could reasonably choose.

reason.description: Why you recommend it, from the request, the code or the evidence.

cost.description: What the recommendation gives up compared with the alternative.

reopenTrigger.description: What would make this worth deciding again.

dependsOn.description: Parent choices this one assumes, each with the parent answer the recommendation was drafted against. If a parent is answered differently, this choice needs review again.

field.description: The spec field this claim joins when a person accepts the choice.

text.description: The outcome, constraint or edge-case behavior, worded as an observable result. For an edgeCase claim this is the expected behavior.

scenario.description: Required for an edgeCase claim: the situation the expected behavior applies to.

claims.description: What accepting the recommendation adds to the spec. They enter outcomes, constraints or edge cases only when a person accepts the choice, so do not also write them into those fields. A saved choice cannot be edited.

id.description: Existing intent id. Pass it back when re-saving an intent you already saved so the file is updated (version bumped, status preserved) instead of replaced. Omit for a new intent.

objective.description: Why this matters — the problem and who has it

currentState.description: How this works today, before the change — existing behavior and workarounds, so the implementation knows what must not regress. Omit for net-new capability.

implementationContext.description: What the repo actually looks like where this change lands: the files and modules involved, what already exists, what it would touch, how to verify it. You are in the working tree — go read it. Markdown, sub-headings welcome. Advisory: it never changes the readiness verdict, it just stops the implementing agent from rediscovering the codebase.

productId.description: Which product this intent belongs to (cloud mode only). Omit it and the server resolves it when the workspace has exactly one real product; if it cannot, the save fails with PRODUCT_REQUIRED and the candidate list, and you should ask the user which one and retry with an explicit id rather than guessing — a GitHub binding hangs off the product, so it decides which repository merge verification applies to.

provider.description: System that owns the saved query, e.g. "posthog"

kind.description: How to interpret the id, e.g. "saved_insight"

id.description: Stable id of the query. An id, never a name — names get renamed and the record then points nowhere.

resultSelector.description: Optional path into a compound provider response

outcomes.description: Observable, testable state changes. The structured form may carry an optional provider-neutral saved-query measurement recipe.

decisions.description: Decisions settled during design + the alternatives ruled out, so the agent does not relitigate them. Omit to keep the existing decisions. Locally a supplied list replaces them ([] clears); connected, supplied decisions are added to the workspace log, which a save never shrinks.

constraints.description: Hard limits the implementation must respect

scope.description: Scope boundaries — what to build and what to avoid

inScope.description: What is in scope for this intent

outOfScope.description: What is explicitly out of scope

checks.description: Feedback-loop checks (preferred over the legacy test buckets)

intentId.description: Check a specific saved intent by id. Ignored when spec is passed.

repoRoot.description: Absolute path of the repository you are working in; Pathmode checks its intent.md, at the root or in its intent/ folder. Pass it when a no-argument call is refused because your MCP client declares no workspace roots, or declares several. Ignored when spec or intentId is passed.

path.description: The intent file to check, when the repository keeps several in intent/ or names it something other than intent.md, e.g. intent/checkout/intent.md. Relative to repoRoot when that is passed, otherwise to the repository a no-argument call resolves; an absolute path is used as is. Ignored when spec or intentId is passed.

tools.name: intent_save
tools.description: Save an intent spec to the repository intent.md — the default choice when you are working inside a repository. With no path it writes the file check_intent_readiness reads: intent.md at the project root, or the single intent.md in an intent/ folder when the root has none. With a Pathmode API key set it ALSO creates or updates the intent in the workspace and records the sync in the file, so the file is the projection of the record rather than a second copy of it. Re-saving the same intent bumps its version and preserves its status; it never silently replaces a different intent. Use create_intent instead when there is no repository to write into.

localDraft.description: Save an unconnected local draft, even with an API key. Use before repository adoption. Cannot detach an already connected file or apply a change request.

path.description: File path, relative to the project root or absolute inside it; ".." out of the project is rejected. Defaults to the intent file check_intent_readiness reads: intent.md at the root, else the single intent/**/intent.md, else a new root intent.md. Required when intent/ holds several; pass an absolute path when several workspace roots each carry an intent.md. The folder must exist.

overwrite.description: Replace the file even when it already holds a DIFFERENT intent. Default false — the save is refused instead, so an unrelated spec is never clobbered.

changeRequestId.description: Structured PM request this save deliberately applies. Requires baseRepoBodyRevision. A productChoices or decisions request is applied by the server from the request itself; save it with no other body edits.

baseRepoBodyRevision.description: Exact base revision carried by the change request. Requires changeRequestId.

tools.name: intent_import
tools.description: Adopt an existing OpenSpec change as the Pathmode intent record. Reads the change folder exactly as the preflight does (proposal.md, spec deltas, design non-goals, verification in tasks.md) and saves it as intent.md — with a workspace key, also as a workspace intent. The change folder is NEVER modified, and field text travels verbatim, so never retype fields from the change yourself. After importing, resolve any unconfirmed dimensions with confirm_intent_dimension.

path.description: OpenSpec change directory, e.g. openspec/changes/add-export. When omitted the repo is scanned: exactly one active change imports directly; several returns the list to pick from.

intentPath.description: Where the intent file is written. Defaults to the repository intent file (intent.md at the root, else the single intent/**/intent.md), and import never replaces one that exists.

overwrite.description: Replace the intent file even when it already holds a DIFFERENT intent. Default false — refused instead.

productId.description: Cloud mode: the product this intent belongs to, when the workspace asks for one.

tools.name: confirm_intent_dimension
tools.description: Resolve an "unconfirmed" readiness dimension, in a local intent.md or in a connected workspace. Use this when check_intent_readiness reports that it READ your objective or outcomes but could not confirm them: the gate matches a fixed English and Finnish vocabulary and misses valid phrasing, including other languages. confirm: state who is affected and what goes wrong for them, in your own words, and the dimension passes. waive: mark the dimension as not applicable to this change (a pure refactor has no product outcome). A waiver is a HUMAN decision, so set humanApproved only after the user has explicitly agreed. Waivers are local-mode only: a workspace will not accept one over an API key, which authenticates as a machine. The confirmation is bound to the exact text it was made against and dies automatically if that text is edited. You cannot confirm a dimension the gate read nothing for; write the field first, save, then confirm.

dimension.description: Only these two are confirmable. Title and verification are never waivable.

action.description: confirm: vouch that the text names what the gate could not find. waive: this dimension does not apply to this change.

actor.description: confirm + objective: who is affected, in your words.

problem.description: confirm + objective: what goes wrong for them today.

observable.description: confirm + outcomes: how you would see it.

reason.description: waive: why this dimension does not apply.

humanApproved.description: waive only. Set ONLY after the user has explicitly approved the waiver. Recorded as a human decision that this environment cannot verify.

path.description: Local mode only: path to the intent file. Defaults to the one check_intent_readiness reads: intent.md at the root, else the single intent/**/intent.md.

intentId.description: Cloud mode: confirm on a specific saved intent. Defaults to the current intent.

tools.name: intent_export
tools.description: Export an intent spec as .cursorrules, a CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md section, a Claude Managed Agents Outcomes rubric, or an OpenSpec change folder. Use agents-md for Codex, Cursor, and other AGENTS.md-aware agents. Use openspec to hand the intent to an OpenSpec workflow: it writes proposal.md, a spec delta, and the verification contract in tasks.md, placed where the preflight reader finds them, and never writes into an existing change.

productChoices.description: New open product choices, never human answers. Existing choices are preserved.

id.description: Stable id for this choice. Never reuse an id for a different question.

question.description: The product decision the request leaves open, asked so a person can answer it.

recommendation.description: The answer you recommend. It stays an assumption until a person accepts it.

alternative.description: The strongest other answer a person could reasonably choose.

reason.description: Why you recommend it, from the request, the code or the evidence.

cost.description: What the recommendation gives up compared with the alternative.

reopenTrigger.description: What would make this worth deciding again.

dependsOn.description: Parent choices this one assumes, each with the parent answer the recommendation was drafted against. If a parent is answered differently, this choice needs review again.

field.description: The spec field this claim joins when a person accepts the choice.

text.description: The outcome, constraint or edge-case behavior, worded as an observable result. For an edgeCase claim this is the expected behavior.

scenario.description: Required for an edgeCase claim: the situation the expected behavior applies to.

claims.description: What accepting the recommendation adds to the spec. They enter outcomes, constraints or edge cases only when a person accepts the choice, so do not also write them into those fields. A saved choice cannot be edited.

id.description: Existing intent id. Pass it back when re-saving an intent you already saved so the file is updated (version bumped, status preserved) instead of replaced. Omit for a new intent.

objective.description: Why this matters — the problem and who has it

currentState.description: How this works today, before the change — existing behavior and workarounds, so the implementation knows what must not regress. Omit for net-new capability.

implementationContext.description: What the repo actually looks like where this change lands: the files and modules involved, what already exists, what it would touch, how to verify it. You are in the working tree — go read it. Markdown, sub-headings welcome. Advisory: it never changes the readiness verdict, it just stops the implementing agent from rediscovering the codebase.

productId.description: Which product this intent belongs to (cloud mode only). Omit it and the server resolves it when the workspace has exactly one real product; if it cannot, the save fails with PRODUCT_REQUIRED and the candidate list, and you should ask the user which one and retry with an explicit id rather than guessing — a GitHub binding hangs off the product, so it decides which repository merge verification applies to.

provider.description: System that owns the saved query, e.g. "posthog"

kind.description: How to interpret the id, e.g. "saved_insight"

id.description: Stable id of the query. An id, never a name — names get renamed and the record then points nowhere.

resultSelector.description: Optional path into a compound provider response

outcomes.description: Observable, testable state changes. The structured form may carry an optional provider-neutral saved-query measurement recipe.

decisions.description: Decisions settled during design + the alternatives ruled out, so the agent does not relitigate them. Omit to keep the existing decisions. Locally a supplied list replaces them ([] clears); connected, supplied decisions are added to the workspace log, which a save never shrinks.

constraints.description: Hard limits the implementation must respect

scope.description: Scope boundaries — what to build and what to avoid

inScope.description: What is in scope for this intent

outOfScope.description: What is explicitly out of scope

checks.description: Feedback-loop checks (preferred over the legacy test buckets)

path.description: Output file path relative to the project root. Must stay inside the project (absolute paths and ".." are rejected). Defaults to .cursorrules, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or openspec/changes/<change-id>

instructions: Pathmode is connected to a workspace (cloud mode). When asked to build, implement, fix, or change product code, first call check_intent_readiness with no arguments for this repository. It resolves intent.md from MCP workspace roots or the server launch directory; never substitute the workspace current intent. Before forming a proposal or implementation plan in connected mode, call list_intents without a status filter and look for relevant earlier decisions on the same product in intents that are authorized, shipped, or verified. Authorization is separate from lifecycle status: an authorized intent can still be draft. Establish the product from the repository binding or the user; if it is ambiguous, ask instead of borrowing another product's decisions. Read applicable decisions and their rationale and reopen triggers; use get_intent when the list lacks the needed detail. In the new intent's existing decisions, record a reason naming the full prior intent ID and full prior decision ID (copy IDs exactly; never abbreviate), or the exact choice if no decision ID is present, its reopen trigger (or that none is recorded), and what it changes about this proposal. Do not claim reuse when nothing applicable was read. If a reopen trigger applies or the earlier decision conflicts with the new request, surface the conflict for a new product judgment. Earlier authorization is context only and never authorizes the new intent or changes to the earlier one. If no intent.md exists, read the actual request and relevant code for discovery, then propose an intent for that request. Record consequential behavior the request leaves undecided as open productChoices: question, recommendation, reason, alternative, cost, reopenTrigger, and contingent claims. Keep recommendations distinct from supplied requirements; do not copy contingent claims into required outcomes or invent choices when the request already settles them. Word each contingent outcome claim as an observable result before the first save: a saved choice cannot be edited. If the preflight flags one as not measurable, say so when you explain the open choices and hand off for review: accepted as written it can fail the outcomes check, and the reviewer can change it in review. Call intent_save with localDraft: true and the complete spec, including those productChoices. Save the draft, rerun check_intent_readiness, explain the open choices, and STOP before changing product code. A terminal question or a plan alone does not preserve the choice. If the repository cannot be identified, ask for its location before saving; never replace a different intent or detach an already connected file. For team review, run npx @pathmode/mcp-server@latest adopt in the repository. It prints a link and a code; give both to the person for browser approval. If it reports AUTHORIZATION_PENDING, stop and rerun the same command after approval. No spec is uploaded before approval. After adoption succeeds, attach the verbatim original request with attach_original_request and provide the review link. Then, if you can run a background command, start node /pkg/node_modules/@pathmode/mcp-server/dist/index.js watch-review --build in the background if the person asked you to implement the change, or node /pkg/node_modules/@pathmode/mcp-server/dist/index.js watch-review --no-build if they asked only for a proposal, tell the person you are listening for their answers, and end the turn; otherwise stop for review. Restart it without either flag after applying answers. If the person changes their mind about building, for example "hold off", leave the background listener running and run node /pkg/node_modules/@pathmode/mcp-server/dist/index.js watch-review --build --declare or node /pkg/node_modules/@pathmode/mcp-server/dist/index.js watch-review --no-build --declare beside it: it records the change for this review and exits, and the listener still reports their answers and verdict. Changing whether to build never means stopping the listener. When it prints a line, follow it: PATHMODE_REVIEW_READY names change requests to apply or reject, then start it again; PATHMODE_REVIEW_WAITING means start it again; the other lines end listening and say what to do. Add --renew only when the person asks you to listen again after PATHMODE_REVIEW_STOPPED. After any authorization, build only once get_agent_prompt with mode "execute" succeeds: if it refuses as not ready, tell the person the blockers it names and do not implement, because an authorization does not accept failed execution checks. An API key alone does not establish repository ownership. For an existing repository intent, preflight still comes before product-code changes. A failing verdict names the exact blockers to repair; explicit acceptance of a named risk does not make the verdict pass. A reviewer answer requests a correction; the agent applies it, and the reviewer separately authorizes the exact resulting revision. Before revising or implementing a repository proposal, call get_review_feedback and address open general change requests; a save must not close them. Product-choice answers, including different answers, arrive through get_change_requests and must be applied through their request IDs. Feedback alone never permits changing a stored choice. Before implementation, check_intent_readiness and get_agent_prompt each print a Revision line comparing intent.md in this repository with the workspace body. Build only when it says intent.md matches the authorized revision (or, for a human-authored intent, the workspace revision); get_agent_prompt with mode "execute" refuses otherwise. Any other Revision line means do not build: it names the repair, such as running node /pkg/node_modules/@pathmode/mcp-server/dist/index.js pull in the repository for a stale file, or saving or discarding local edits. A pull of an unauthorized revision does not permit a build. Stop for pending corrections or missing, rejected, or stale authorization. When the revision is waiting for a person's approval and you can run a background command, start node /pkg/node_modules/@pathmode/mcp-server/dist/index.js watch-review --build in the background if they asked you to implement it, or node /pkg/node_modules/@pathmode/mcp-server/dist/index.js watch-review --no-build if they asked only for a proposal, and end the turn instead of polling or setting timers: when they approve, it brings intent.md to the approved revision and prints one line saying what to do. If tools fail with API error (401), the configured key is invalid: re-run npx @pathmode/mcp-server setup with a fresh key from your workspace settings at https://pathmode.io, or remove PATHMODE_API_KEY and restart to fall back to free keyless local mode (specs live in intent.md, no account needed).
